svg.title: Binary Search
svg.desc: Binary Search. Halve a sorted range with every check: about 20 steps find one item among a million, where a scan may need a million. Step 1, Scan one by one: A linear scan checks cells from the left: 58 takes 13 checks, and a missing value takes all 16. Step 2, Halve the range: Binary search checks the middle and drops the half that can't hold 58: found after 4 checks. Step 3, A miss lands somewhere: Find 50: after 4 checks lo has passed hi, so 50 is absent, and lo = 11 is where it would go. Step 4, Why it scales: Each check halves the range: 20 checks cover a million items, but only on sorted, indexable data.

g.text: A linear scan checks cells from the left: 58 takes 13 checks, and a missing value takes all 16.
Binary search checks the middle and drops the half that can't hold 58: found after 4 checks.
Find 50: after 4 checks lo has passed hi, so 50 is absent, and lo = 11 is where it would go.
Each check halves the range: 20 checks cover a million items, but only on sorted, indexable data.
Linear scan: compare a[i] with the target for i = 0, 1, 2, … until one matches
Each miss rules out just one cell, so the worst case is n checks: O(n).

text.tspan: after 13 checks, one per cell from index 0.

g.text: A missing value is the worst case: the scan checks all 16 cells before it gives up.
Binary search: check the middle, mid = (lo + hi) // 2, and keep only the half that can still hold the target

text.tspan: lo = 11 > hi = 10: the range is empty, so
to keep the order, as bisect_left(a, 50) = 11 says.

g.text: Worst case for 16 cells: each check halves the range
Checks needed in the worst case
binary search: ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 checks at most; a scan: up to n
fast access by index: not a linked list
The first form sat in the JDK for about nine years (Bloch, 2006).
